subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw allow operator-configured custom headers to survive cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and if yes must that permission be scoped by destination origin instead of a global header-name allowlist?
rationale: This changes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public security/config surface, so automation cannot choose the trust model or acceptable guardrails.

options.title: Design scoped operator policy
options.body: Add the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, documentation, and tests that prove strict default behavior remains unchanged.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and keep custom credential-like headers blocked on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add global header extension list
options.body: Implement the requested header-name-only config while accepting the higher risk that an allowed header can be replayed to any redirect origin.

recommendation.title: Design scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Add the capability only with header-name validation, destination-origin scoping, documentation, and tests that prove strict default behavior remains unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The strict behavior traces to steipete's security hardening commit, and the remaining choice is whether to relax that boundary.
